source.text: Ὁμοίως γυναῖκες ὑποτασσόμεναι τοῖς ἰδίοις ἀνδράσιν, ἵνα καὶ εἴ τινες ἀπειθοῦσιν τῷ λόγῳ διὰ τῆς τῶν γυναικῶν ἀναστροφῆς ἄνευ λόγου κερδηθήσονται ἐποπτεύσαντες τὴν ἐν φόβῳ ἁγνὴν ἀναστροφὴν ὑμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Likewise wives being subject to the own husbands, so that even if any disobey the word, through the of the wives conduct without word they will be gained, \v 2 having observed the in fear pure conduct of you.

en.L: Likewise, wives, [be] subject to [your] own husbands, so that even if some disobey the word, they will be won without a word through the conduct of [their] wives, \v 2 having observed your pure conduct in fear.
en.B: In the same way, wives, submit to your own husbands. Then if any of them do not obey the word, your way of life will win them over even without your saying a word, \v 2 as they watch how pure your conduct is and how you live in reverence for God.
en.R: Wives, in the same way, accept the authority of your own husbands. Some of your husbands may not believe God's message. But they can still be won over to it, without you saying a word, just by the way you live. \v 2 They will see that your life is pure and that you live with deep respect for God.

es.L: Asimismo, esposas, [{{plural_you:estén|estad}}] sometidas a {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} propios esposos, para que, aun si algunos desobedecen a la palabra, sean ganados sin palabra por medio de la conducta de [sus] esposas, \v 2 al observar {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} conducta pura en temor.
es.B: Del mismo modo, esposas, {{plural_you:sométanse|someteos}} a {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} propios esposos. Así, si algunos de ellos no obedecen a la palabra, {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} manera de vivir los ganará, aun sin que {{plural_you:ustedes digan|vosotras digáis}} una palabra, \v 2 cuando vean lo pura que es {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} conducta y cómo {{plural_you:viven|vivís}} en reverencia a Dios.
es.R: Esposas, de la misma manera, {{plural_you:sométanse|someteos}} a la autoridad de {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} propios esposos. Puede que algunos de {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} esposos no crean el mensaje de Dios. Pero aun así pueden ser ganados para ese mensaje, sin que {{plural_you:ustedes digan|vosotras digáis}} nada, solo por la manera en que {{plural_you:viven|vivís}}. \v 2 Ellos verán que {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} vida es pura y que {{plural_you:viven|vivís}} con profundo respeto a Dios.

fr.L: De même, femmes, [soyez] soumises à [vos] propres maris, afin que, même si quelques-uns désobéissent à la parole, ils soient gagnés sans parole par la conduite de [leurs] femmes, \v 2 ayant observé votre conduite pure dans la crainte.
fr.B: De même, vous, les femmes, soumettez-vous à votre mari. Alors, si certains d’entre eux n’obéissent pas à la parole, votre manière de vivre les gagnera, sans même que vous ayez à dire un mot, \v 2 quand ils verront combien votre conduite est pure et combien vous vivez dans le respect de Dieu.
fr.R: Vous, les femmes, de la même façon, acceptez l’autorité de votre mari. Certains de vos maris ne croient peut-être pas au message de Dieu. Mais ils peuvent quand même être gagnés à ce message, sans que vous disiez un mot, simplement par votre manière de vivre. \v 2 Ils verront que votre vie est pure et que vous vivez avec un profond respect pour Dieu.

sw.L: Vivyo hivyo, wake, [wanyenyekeeni] waume zenu wenyewe, ili hata kama wengine hawalitii neno, watavutwa bila neno kupitia mwenendo wa wake [zao], \v 2 wakiwa wameuona mwenendo wenu safi katika hofu.
sw.B: Vivyo hivyo, wake, wanyenyekeeni waume zenu wenyewe. Hivyo, kama baadhi yao hawalitii neno, mwenendo wenu utawavuta hata bila ninyi kusema neno, \v 2 watakapoona jinsi mwenendo wenu ulivyo safi na jinsi mnavyomcha Mungu.
sw.R: Wake, vivyo hivyo, wanyenyekeeni waume zenu wenyewe. Huenda baadhi ya waume zenu hawauamini ujumbe wa Mungu. Lakini bado wanaweza kuvutwa waupokee, bila ninyi kusema neno, kwa jinsi tu mnavyoishi. \v 2 Wataona kwamba maisha yenu ni safi na kwamba mnaishi mkimheshimu Mungu sana.

decisions.choice: be subject: a participle used as a command, continuing the instructions that began at 2:13
alternatives: a participle that depends on a command in 2:18 or 2:13
decisions.reason: ὑποτασσόμεναι is a participle, but it stands where a command is expected, as ὑποτάσσω does for slaves in 2:18. Ὁμοίως, "likewise", ties it to the call in 2:13 to be subject to every human institution "for the Lord's sake", and to the example of Christ in 2:21-25. It compares the kind of conduct asked for, not the position of a wife to that of a slave.

decisions.choice: wives who have believed, some of them married to husbands who have not
decisions.reason: In Greek and Roman households a wife was expected to share her husband's gods. A wife who followed Christ when her husband did not was already going against that expectation, and Peter does not tell her to give up her faith. What the text asks is that she be subject to her own husband (ἰδίοις, "own"), not to men in general, and that she win him by how she lives rather than by pressing him with words. It does not tell her to obey him in anything that would mean denying Christ, and it does not say what she should do if he harms her; 3:6 tells her not to be ruled by fear.

decisions.choice: the passage gives a purpose for the wife's conduct: that unbelieving husbands may be won for Christ
alternatives: the passage grounds submission only in the order of creation
the passage grounds submission only in the needs of the first readers' setting
decisions.reason: The ἵνα clause states a purpose: "so that ... they will be won". Peter also grounds the conduct in 2:13 ("for the Lord's sake") and in the example of the holy women and Sarah (3:5-6). How far this instruction is tied to the household customs of the first readers, and how it applies in other settings, is debated among Christians; the translation reports what the text says and leaves that question open.

decisions.choice: the word ... without a word: the message of the gospel, then the wives' own words
decisions.reason: Peter plays on λόγος. τῷ λόγῳ is the word of God that was preached to them (1:23-25; 2:8). ἄνευ λόγου means without speech: the wives do not need to argue their husbands into faith. It does not mean without the gospel.

decisions.choice: won: gained for Christ, brought to faith
decisions.reason: κερδαίνω means to gain or profit; Paul uses it for winning people to Christ (1 Corinthians 9:19-22), and Jesus for winning back a brother (Matthew 18:15). The future tense states what Peter expects can happen.

decisions.choice: in fear: in reverence for God; pure: morally clean, chaste
decisions.reason: Throughout the letter φόβος is reverence toward God (1:17; 2:17-18). It cannot mean fear of the husband, since 3:6 tells the wives not to fear anything and 3:14 says the same to everyone. ἁγνὴν describes a life that is morally pure and faithful in marriage.

decisions.choice: be subject (L); submit (B); accept the authority of (R)
decisions.reason: ὑποτάσσω means to place oneself under another's authority. "Obey" is a different word in Greek (used of Sarah in 3:6); Readable explains the idea in plain words.

decisions.choice: reverence for God (B); deep respect for God (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name whom the fear is toward (m6), so that readers do not take it as fear of the husband.

decisions.choice: may not believe God's message ... won over to it
decisions.reason: To disobey the word is to refuse the gospel (2:8); Readable says this plainly and names what they are won to.

decisions.choice: ustedes / vosotras forms
decisions.reason: Peter writes to the churches in the plural throughout the letter. Each plural "you" and its verb is a reader setting: ustedes (Latin America, the default) or vosotros (Spain), as in Paul's letters. Here the wives are addressed, so the Spain form is "vosotras".

decisions.choice: esposas, esposos; sometidas (L), someterse (B), someterse a la autoridad de (R)
decisions.reason: As in Ephesians 5:22, "esposa" and "esposo" make plain that wives and husbands are meant, and "someterse" is the word used there for this verb. Readable adds "a la autoridad de" to say what submitting means.

decisions.choice: kunyenyekea
decisions.reason: "Kunyenyekea" (to place oneself under) is the word used for this verb in Ephesians 5:22. "Kutii" (obey) is kept for the different Greek word used of Sarah in 3:6.

decisions.choice: watavutwa (L), kuwavuta (B, R); hofu (L), kumcha Mungu (B), kumheshimu Mungu (R)
decisions.reason: "Kupatwa" (to be gained) is not said of people in Swahili; "kuvuta" is the usual word for winning someone over to faith. For φόβῳ, Balanced uses the Swahili idiom "kumcha Mungu", which means reverence for God and cannot be taken as fear of the husband.

source.text: ὧν ἔστω οὐχ ὁ ἔξωθεν ἐμπλοκῆς τριχῶν καὶ περιθέσεως χρυσίων ἢ ἐνδύσεως ἱματίων κόσμος, ἀλλ’ ὁ κρυπτὸς τῆς καρδίας ἄνθρωπος ἐν τῷ ἀφθάρτῳ τοῦ πραέως καὶ ἡσυχίου πνεύματος, ὅ ἐστιν ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ πολυτελές.

records.literal_gloss: Of whom let be not the outward of braiding of hairs and of putting around of gold [things] or of putting on of garments adornment, \v 4 but the hidden of the heart person in the imperishable of the gentle and quiet spirit, which is before the God costly.

en.L: Let your adornment be not the outward [kind], of braiding of hair and putting on of gold [ornaments] or wearing of clothes, \v 4 but the hidden person of the heart, in the imperishable [adornment] of a gentle and quiet spirit, which is costly before God.
en.B: Do not let your adornment be the outward kind: braided hair, gold ornaments, and the clothes you put on. \v 4 Let it be the hidden self of the heart, adorned with what never decays, a gentle and quiet spirit, which God values highly.
en.R: Do not think that what makes you beautiful is on the outside: the way you braid your hair, the gold jewelry you wear, or your clothes. \v 4 Your beauty should come from deep inside, from who you are in your heart. A gentle and quiet spirit is a beauty that will never decay, and God thinks it is worth a great deal.

es.L: Que {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} adorno no sea el exterior, de trenzado de cabellos y de colocación de [joyas de] oro o de vestido de ropas, \v 4 sino la persona oculta del corazón, en el [adorno] incorruptible de un espíritu manso y sereno, que es de gran precio delante de Dios.
es.B: Que {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} adorno no sea el exterior: peinados trenzados, joyas de oro y la ropa que {{plural_you:se ponen|os ponéis}}. \v 4 Que sea la persona escondida en el corazón, adornada con lo que nunca se deteriora: un espíritu manso y sereno, que Dios valora mucho.
es.R: No {{plural_you:piensen|penséis}} que lo que {{plural_you:las|os}} hace hermosas está por fuera: la manera de trenzar{{plural_you:se|os}} el cabello, las joyas de oro que {{plural_you:llevan|lleváis}} o {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} ropa. \v 4 {{plural_you:Su|Vuestra}} belleza debe venir de muy adentro, de lo que {{plural_you:son|sois}} en el corazón. Un espíritu manso y sereno es una belleza que nunca se marchita, y Dios lo considera de muchísimo valor.

fr.L: Que votre parure ne soit pas celle du dehors, [celle] des cheveux tressés, des bijoux d’or qu’on met ou des vêtements qu’on porte, \v 4 mais la personne cachée du cœur, dans la [parure] impérissable d’un esprit doux et paisible, qui est d’un grand prix devant Dieu.
fr.B: Que votre parure ne soit pas extérieure : cheveux tressés, bijoux d’or, vêtements que l’on porte. \v 4 Qu’elle soit plutôt l’être intérieur caché dans le cœur, paré de ce qui ne se gâte jamais, un esprit doux et paisible, auquel Dieu accorde un grand prix.
fr.R: Ne pensez pas que ce qui vous rend belles se trouve à l’extérieur : votre façon de vous tresser les cheveux, les bijoux d’or que vous portez ou vos vêtements. \v 4 Votre beauté doit venir du plus profond de vous-mêmes, de ce que vous êtes dans votre cœur. Un esprit doux et paisible est une beauté qui ne s’abîmera jamais, et Dieu trouve qu’elle a une grande valeur.

sw.L: Pambo lenu lisiwe la nje, la kusuka nywele na kuvaa [vito vya] dhahabu au kuvaa mavazi, \v 4 bali mtu aliyefichika wa moyo, katika [pambo] lisiloharibika la roho ya upole na ya utulivu, ambalo ni la thamani kubwa mbele za Mungu.
sw.B: Pambo lenu lisiwe la nje: nywele zilizosukwa, vito vya dhahabu na nguo mnazovaa. \v 4 Bali liwe utu wa ndani uliofichika moyoni, uliopambwa kwa kitu kisichoharibika kamwe, yaani roho ya upole na ya utulivu, ambayo Mungu anaithamini sana.
sw.R: Msidhani kwamba kinachowafanya mpendeze ni vitu vya nje: jinsi mnavyosuka nywele zenu, vito vya dhahabu mnavyovaa, au nguo zenu. \v 4 Uzuri wenu unapaswa kutoka ndani kabisa, katika jinsi mlivyo moyoni. Roho ya upole na ya utulivu ni uzuri usiochakaa kamwe, na Mungu anauona kuwa wa thamani kubwa sana.

decisions.choice: adornment: what a person puts on to look beautiful
decisions.reason: κόσμος first meant order or arrangement, and so decoration. Here it is the wives' adornment, and the verb from the same root returns in 3:5 (ἐκόσμουν, "adorned themselves"). It does not have its other sense, the world, in this verse.

decisions.choice: not ... but: a contrast of what matters most, not a ban on hair styles, jewelry or clothes
alternatives: a rule against braided hair and gold jewelry
decisions.reason: Clothing itself is on the list, so the sentence cannot forbid everything it names. A "not this but that" contrast often says which of two things counts, and here it tells the wives where their real beauty lies. The text does not lay down rules about dress.

decisions.choice: braided hair, gold, and fine clothing: the costly display of wealth and status
decisions.reason: Elaborate hair woven with gold and expensive clothing were marks of wealth in the Greek and Roman world, and moral writers of the time, Jewish and non-Jewish, urged wives not to rely on them. 1 Timothy 2:9-10 gives similar advice.

decisions.choice: the hidden person of the heart: the inner self, the person as God sees them
decisions.reason: ἄνθρωπος here is the human person, man or woman. The "hidden" self is the character that cannot be seen, set against the "outward" adornment of 3:3.

decisions.choice: in the imperishable: the adornment that does not decay, in contrast to gold
decisions.reason: ἀφθάρτῳ has no noun; the context supplies "adornment". The letter uses the same word for the inheritance and the seed of new birth that never perish (1:4, 1:23) and contrasts them with gold that perishes (1:7, 1:18).

decisions.choice: a gentle and quiet spirit: a person's disposition, not the Holy Spirit
decisions.reason: πνεύματος here is the inner temper of a person. πραέως is gentle, the word Jesus uses of himself in Matthew 11:29; ἡσυχίου is calm and settled, not anxious or quarrelsome (1 Timothy 2:2). It does not mean silent.

decisions.choice: costly: of great value
decisions.reason: πολυτελές means very expensive. Peter sets it against the costly gold and clothing of 3:3: this is the adornment God counts as precious.

decisions.choice: adornment (L, B); what makes you beautiful, beauty (R)
decisions.reason: The word means adornment here (m1). Readable says what adornment is for.

decisions.choice: the hidden self
decisions.reason: "Self" keeps the sense of the whole person without implying a male person, since the verse speaks to wives.

decisions.choice: persona
decisions.reason: ἄνθρωπος here is the human person (meaning decision), and the verse speaks to wives; "persona" says this, where "hombre" would suggest a man.

decisions.choice: la personne cachée du cœur (L); l’être intérieur caché dans le cœur (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is the one for a human being; the verse speaks to wives, so French "l’homme" would read as "the man". "La personne" and "l’être intérieur" keep the whole inner self (m4), as the English "self" does.

decisions.choice: utu wa ndani
decisions.reason: "Utu" is a person's inner self or character, which is what the hidden person of the heart means; Literal keeps "mtu", the word in the Greek.

source.text: οὕτως γάρ ποτε καὶ αἱ ἅγιαι γυναῖκες αἱ ἐλπίζουσαι εἰς θεὸν ἐκόσμουν ἑαυτάς, ὑποτασσόμεναι τοῖς ἰδίοις ἀνδράσιν, ὡς Σάρρα ὑπήκουσεν τῷ Ἀβραάμ, κύριον αὐτὸν καλοῦσα· ἧς ἐγενήθητε τέκνα ἀγαθοποιοῦσαι καὶ μὴ φοβούμεναι μηδεμίαν πτόησιν.

records.literal_gloss: For thus once also the holy women the [ones] hoping in God were adorning themselves, being subject to the own husbands, \v 6 as Sarah obeyed the Abraham, lord him calling; of whom you became children, doing good and not fearing any terror.

en.L: For in this way also the holy women of old who hoped in God used to adorn themselves, being subject to their own husbands, \v 6 as Sarah obeyed Abraham, calling him lord. You have become her children, doing good and not fearing any terror.
en.B: This is how the holy women of the past who put their hope in God made themselves beautiful: they submitted to their own husbands. \v 6 So Sarah obeyed Abraham and called him her lord. You have become her daughters, as long as you do what is good and let nothing terrify you.
en.R: Long ago, the holy women who trusted in God made themselves beautiful in this same way. They accepted the authority of their own husbands. \v 6 Sarah was like this. She obeyed Abraham and called him "my lord." You have become her daughters if you do what is good and do not let anything frighten you.

es.L: Porque así también en otro tiempo las santas mujeres que esperaban en Dios se adornaban a sí mismas, estando sometidas a sus propios esposos, \v 6 como Sara obedeció a Abraham, llamándolo señor. De ella {{plural_you:han|habéis}} llegado a ser hijas, haciendo el bien y no temiendo ningún espanto.
es.B: Así es como las santas mujeres del pasado, que ponían su esperanza en Dios, se hacían hermosas: se sometían a sus propios esposos. \v 6 Así Sara obedeció a Abraham y lo llamó su señor. {{plural_you:Ustedes han|Vosotras habéis}} llegado a ser hijas de ella, siempre que {{plural_you:hagan|hagáis}} el bien y no {{plural_you:se dejen|os dejéis}} aterrorizar por nada.
es.R: Hace mucho tiempo, las santas mujeres que confiaban en Dios se hacían hermosas de esta misma manera. Se sometían a la autoridad de sus propios esposos. \v 6 Así era Sara. Ella obedeció a Abraham y lo llamó «mi señor». {{plural_you:Ustedes han|Vosotras habéis}} llegado a ser sus hijas si {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} lo bueno y no {{plural_you:dejan|dejáis}} que nada {{plural_you:las|os}} asuste.

fr.L: Car c’est ainsi qu’autrefois aussi les saintes femmes qui espéraient en Dieu se paraient, étant soumises à leurs propres maris, \v 6 comme Sara a obéi à Abraham, l’appelant seigneur. Vous êtes devenues ses enfants, en faisant le bien et en ne vous laissant troubler par aucune frayeur.
fr.B: C’est ainsi que les saintes femmes d’autrefois, qui mettaient leur espérance en Dieu, se rendaient belles : elles étaient soumises à leur mari. \v 6 C’est ainsi que Sara a obéi à Abraham et l’a appelé son seigneur. Vous êtes devenues ses filles, pourvu que vous fassiez le bien et que vous ne vous laissiez effrayer par rien.
fr.R: Il y a longtemps, les saintes femmes qui comptaient sur Dieu se rendaient belles de cette même manière. Elles acceptaient l’autorité de leur mari. \v 6 Sara était comme cela. Elle a obéi à Abraham et l’a appelé « mon seigneur ». Vous êtes devenues ses filles si vous faites ce qui est bien et si vous ne laissez rien vous faire peur.

sw.L: Kwa maana hivyo ndivyo zamani wanawake watakatifu waliomtumaini Mungu walivyojipamba pia, wakiwanyenyekea waume zao wenyewe, \v 6 kama Sara alivyomtii Ibrahimu, akimwita bwana. Ninyi mmekuwa watoto wake, mkitenda mema na kutoogopa kitisho chochote.
sw.B: Hivi ndivyo wanawake watakatifu wa zamani, waliomtumaini Mungu, walivyojipamba: waliwanyenyekea waume zao wenyewe. \v 6 Ndivyo Sara alivyomtii Ibrahimu, akamwita bwana wake. Ninyi mmekuwa binti zake, ikiwa mnatenda mema bila kutishwa na kitu chochote.
sw.R: Zamani sana, wanawake watakatifu waliomtumaini Mungu walijipamba kwa njia hii hii. Waliwanyenyekea waume zao wenyewe. \v 6 Sara alikuwa hivyo. Alimtii Ibrahimu na kumwita "bwana wangu." Ninyi mmekuwa binti zake, ikiwa mnatenda yaliyo mema na hamuogopi kitu chochote.

decisions.choice: the holy women: the women of Israel's past who belonged to God, such as the wives of the patriarchs
decisions.reason: ἅγιαι means set apart for God. Peter names one of them, Sarah, the mother of Israel. What made them holy was their hope in God, the same hope the letter calls its readers to (1:3, 1:13, 1:21).

decisions.choice: calling him lord: Genesis 18:12, where Sarah speaks of Abraham as "my lord"
decisions.reason: In Genesis 18:12 Sarah, laughing to herself at the promise of a son, calls Abraham "my lord". It was a respectful way for a wife to speak of her husband, like "sir" or "master", not a title of worship. Peter draws on Sarah's respect for Abraham; he does not say she obeyed in everything, and Genesis also shows Abraham listening to Sarah (Genesis 16:2; 21:12).

decisions.choice: you have become her children: believers who were not born Jewish now belong to Sarah's family
decisions.reason: Many of the readers had been Gentiles (1:14, 1:18; 4:3). As Paul says that those who believe are children of Abraham (Galatians 3:7, 3:29; compare Galatians 4:28-31 and Isaiah 51:2), Peter says these wives have become Sarah's children. ἐγενήθητε looks back to the time they became believers.

decisions.choice: doing good and not fearing: the conduct that shows they are her children
alternatives: a condition: if you do good
the reason: because you do good
decisions.reason: The participles can state a condition for being Sarah's children or describe how they show it. Either way, doing good and refusing to be ruled by fear is what marks them as her family.

decisions.choice: not fearing any terror: an echo of Proverbs 3:25
decisions.reason: The phrase recalls Proverbs 3:25 in the Greek Old Testament, which also has πτόησιν: do not be afraid of sudden terror. For wives with unbelieving husbands the threat could come from the household itself. Peter tells them not to be intimidated, as he tells the whole church in 3:14.

decisions.choice: daughters
decisions.reason: τέκνα is "children"; the people meant are the wives Peter is addressing, so Balanced and Readable say "daughters". Literal keeps "children".

decisions.choice: made themselves beautiful
decisions.reason: Keeps the link with the adornment of 3:3-4 in everyday words. Literal keeps "adorn".

decisions.choice: hijas
decisions.reason: τέκνα is "children", and English Literal keeps that word. Spanish has no word for children that is not masculine in form, and "hijos" said to the wives would sound as if it meant sons, so all three levels say "hijas".

decisions.choice: bwana, lowercase
decisions.reason: Swahili uses one word for "lord" and "sir". Sarah's word for her husband is ordinary respectful address (meaning decision), so it is written lowercase, as polite "bwana" is, and not with the capital kept for the Lord.

source.text: Οἱ ἄνδρες ὁμοίως συνοικοῦντες κατὰ γνῶσιν, ὡς ἀσθενεστέρῳ σκεύει τῷ γυναικείῳ ἀπονέμοντες τιμήν, ὡς καὶ συγκληρονόμοις χάριτος ζωῆς, εἰς τὸ μὴ ἐγκόπτεσθαι τὰς προσευχὰς ὑμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: The husbands likewise, living with [them] according to knowledge, as with a weaker vessel, the female, assigning honor, as also co-heirs of grace of life, for the not to be hindered the prayers of you.

en.L: Husbands, likewise, live with [your wives] according to knowledge, assigning honor to the female as to a weaker vessel, as also co-heirs of [the] grace of life, so that your prayers may not be hindered.
en.B: Husbands, in the same way, live with your wives with understanding. Give honor to the woman as the weaker vessel, and as one who will inherit the grace of life together with you, so that nothing stands in the way of your prayers.
en.R: Husbands, in the same way, live with your wives in an understanding way. Your wife may be weaker than you are, so treat her with honor. God will give her life as a gift of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} grace, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will give it to you. Do this so that nothing will get in the way of your prayers.

es.L: Esposos, asimismo, {{plural_you:convivan|convivid}} [con {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} esposas] según conocimiento, dando honra a la mujer como a vaso más débil, como también a coherederas de [la] gracia de [la] vida, para que {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} oraciones no sean estorbadas.
es.B: Del mismo modo, esposos, {{plural_you:vivan|vivid}} con {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} esposas con comprensión. {{plural_you:Den|Dad}} honra a la mujer como al vaso más débil, y como a quien heredará junto con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} la gracia de la vida, para que nada estorbe {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} oraciones.
es.R: Esposos, de la misma manera, {{plural_you:vivan|vivid}} con {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} esposas con comprensión. Puede que ellas sean más débiles que {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}; por eso, {{plural_you:trátenlas|tratadlas}} con honra. Dios dará también a ellas la vida como regalo de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} gracia, igual que a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. {{plural_you:Háganlo|Hacedlo}} así para que nada se interponga en {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} oraciones.

fr.L: Maris, de même, vivez avec [elles] selon la connaissance, accordant de l’honneur, comme à un vase plus faible, au [vase] féminin, comme aussi à des cohéritières de la grâce de la vie, afin que vos prières ne soient pas entravées.
fr.B: Vous, les maris, de même, vivez avec vos femmes en faisant preuve de compréhension. Honorez la femme comme le vase plus faible, et comme celle qui héritera avec vous de la grâce de la vie, afin que rien ne fasse obstacle à vos prières.
fr.R: Vous, les maris, de la même façon, vivez avec votre femme en la comprenant. Votre femme est peut-être plus faible que vous, alors traitez-la avec honneur. Dieu va lui donner la vie comme un cadeau de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} grâce, tout comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} va vous la donner à vous. Faites cela pour que rien ne vienne gêner vos prières.

sw.L: Waume, vivyo hivyo, kaeni [na wake zenu] kwa kadiri ya maarifa, mkimpa mwanamke heshima kama chombo dhaifu zaidi, kama warithi pamoja [nanyi] wa neema ya uzima, ili maombi yenu yasizuiliwe.
sw.B: Vivyo hivyo, waume, kaeni na wake zenu kwa ufahamu. Mpeni mwanamke heshima kama chombo kilicho dhaifu zaidi, na kama mtu atakayerithi pamoja nanyi neema ya uzima, ili kusiwe na kitu kinachozuia maombi yenu.
sw.R: Waume, vivyo hivyo, kaeni na wake zenu kwa namna ya kuwaelewa. Huenda wake zenu ni dhaifu kuliko ninyi, kwa hiyo waheshimuni. Mungu atawapa wao uzima kama zawadi ya neema {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, kama atakavyowapa ninyi. Fanyeni hivyo ili kusiwe na kitu kitakachozuia maombi yenu.

decisions.choice: likewise: husbands too are given conduct to follow, in the same spirit as 2:13-3:6
decisions.reason: ὁμοίως links the husbands to the same call that the wives received. The participles συνοικοῦντες and ἀπονέμοντες are used as commands, as in 3:1. In the household rules of the time a husband was rarely told what he owed his wife; Peter tells him.

decisions.choice: according to knowledge: with understanding, both of God's will and of his wife
alternatives: with knowledge of the faith only
decisions.reason: γνῶσιν is knowledge or understanding. The husband is to live with his wife in a way that is informed: aware of what God asks and of her situation and needs.

decisions.choice: the weaker vessel goes with assigning honor: honor her because she is the weaker
alternatives: it goes with living together: live with her knowing she is the weaker vessel
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT puts a comma after "according to knowledge", which joins "as with a weaker vessel" to "assigning honor". The phrase can also be read with "living with". On either reading the weakness is a reason for considerate care and honor, not for control.

decisions.choice: weaker vessel: weaker in physical strength, and with less power in society; not weaker in mind, faith or worth
decisions.reason: σκεύει is a vessel or jar, a common picture for a person or body (1 Thessalonians 4:4; 2 Corinthians 4:7). The comparative ἀσθενεστέρῳ implies that the husband is a vessel too, only a stronger one. The text does not say in what way the wife is weaker. In that world a wife had less physical strength and far less legal and social power than her husband. The same sentence calls her a co-heir of the grace of life, so it cannot mean she is less in God's sight.

decisions.choice: co-heirs of the grace of life: wife and husband receive the same inheritance from God
decisions.reason: συγκληρονόμοις means heirs together. The "grace of life" is the life God gives as a gift, the inheritance kept in heaven (1:3-4). Before God the wife stands as an equal heir with her husband.

decisions.choice: your prayers: the husbands' prayers
alternatives: the prayers of husband and wife together
decisions.reason: ὑμῶν is plural. Since the sentence speaks to husbands, it most likely means the husbands' prayers, which God will not hear if they dishonor their wives (3:12). It may also include the prayers the couple make together.

decisions.choice: the weaker vessel
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of the vessel, which implies both are vessels (m4); "sex" would narrow the sense to something the text does not say.

decisions.choice: God will give her life as a gift of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} grace, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will give it to you
alternatives: co-heirs of the grace of life
decisions.reason: Readable unpacks "co-heirs" and "grace of life" (m5) into plain words and keeps the key word grace.

decisions.choice: plural throughout: sus esposas ... más débiles que ustedes
alternatives: tu esposa ... más débil que tú
decisions.reason: English Readable turns to each husband with a singular "your wife". Spanish keeps the plural, as the Greek does, so that the ustedes / vosotros setting applies to the whole verse and the address does not switch between "tú" and "ustedes".

decisions.choice: comme aussi à des cohéritières
decisions.reason: French must mark gender on the noun. The Greek word is in the same case as "the female" and is said of the wives, who inherit with their husbands (m5), so Literal uses the feminine "cohéritières"; Balanced says "celle qui héritera avec vous".

decisions.choice: maarifa (L), ufahamu (B)
decisions.reason: "Ujuzi" is kept for ἐπίγνωσις, as in Colossians and 2 Peter. γνῶσιν here is practical understanding of God's will and of one's wife (meaning decision), so Literal says "maarifa" and Balanced "ufahamu".

source.text: Τὸ δὲ τέλος πάντες ὁμόφρονες, συμπαθεῖς, φιλάδελφοι, εὔσπλαγχνοι, ταπεινόφρονες, μὴ ἀποδιδόντες κακὸν ἀντὶ κακοῦ ἢ λοιδορίαν ἀντὶ λοιδορίας τοὐναντίον δὲ εὐλογοῦντες, ὅτι εἰς τοῦτο ἐκλήθητε ἵνα εὐλογίαν κληρονομήσητε.

records.literal_gloss: And the end, all [be] like-minded, sympathetic, brother-loving, tenderhearted, humble-minded, \v 9 not paying back evil for evil or insult for insult, but on the contrary blessing, because for this you were called, so that a blessing you may inherit.

en.L: Finally, all [of you be] like-minded, sympathetic, loving [one another as] {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, tenderhearted, humble-minded, \v 9 not paying back evil for evil or insult for insult, but on the contrary blessing, because you were called for this, so that you may inherit a blessing.
en.B: To sum up: all of you, be united in mind, share one another's feelings, love each other as {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, be tender in heart and humble in mind. \v 9 Do not pay back evil with evil or abuse with abuse. Instead, bless, because this is what you were called to, so that you may inherit a blessing.
en.R: Finally, all of you should agree with one another and care about one another's feelings. Love each other like {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}. Be kind and gentle, and do not think too highly of yourselves. \v 9 When someone does wrong to you, do not do wrong back. When someone insults you, do not insult them back. Instead, ask God to bless them. God called you to live this way, so that you yourselves will receive God's blessing.

es.L: Finalmente, todos [{{plural_you:sean|sed}}] de un mismo pensar, compasivos, amantes de los hermanos, de corazón tierno, humildes de mente, \v 9 no pagando mal por mal ni insulto por insulto, sino, al contrario, bendiciendo, porque para esto {{plural_you:fueron|fuisteis}} llamados, para que {{plural_you:hereden|heredéis}} una bendición.
es.B: En resumen, {{plural_you:tengan|tened}} todos un mismo modo de pensar, {{plural_you:compartan|compartid}} los sentimientos unos de otros, {{plural_you:ámense|amaos}} como hermanos, {{plural_you:sean|sed}} tiernos de corazón y humildes de mente. \v 9 No {{plural_you:paguen|paguéis}} mal con mal ni ofensa con ofensa. Al contrario, {{plural_you:bendigan|bendecid}}, porque a esto {{plural_you:fueron|fuisteis}} llamados, para que {{plural_you:hereden|heredéis}} una bendición.
es.R: Finalmente, {{plural_you:pónganse|poneos}} todos de acuerdo unos con otros y {{plural_you:preocúpense|preocupaos}} por lo que sienten los demás. {{plural_you:Ámense|Amaos}} como hermanos. {{plural_you:Sean|Sed}} amables y bondadosos, y no {{plural_you:se crean|os creáis}} más importantes que los demás. \v 9 Cuando alguien {{plural_you:les|os}} haga mal, no le {{plural_you:devuelvan|devolváis}} el mal. Cuando alguien {{plural_you:los|os}} insulte, no lo {{plural_you:insulten|insultéis}} a su vez. Más bien, {{plural_you:pídanle|pedidle}} a Dios que bendiga a esas personas. Dios {{plural_you:los|os}} llamó a vivir así, para que {{plural_you:ustedes mismos reciban|vosotros mismos recibáis}} la bendición de Dios.

fr.L: Enfin, [soyez] tous d’un même sentiment, compatissants, vous aimant [comme des] {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, pleins de tendresse, humbles, \v 9 ne rendant pas le mal pour le mal ou l’insulte pour l’insulte, mais au contraire bénissant, car c’est à cela que vous avez été appelés, afin d’hériter une bénédiction.
fr.B: En résumé, soyez tous unis dans les mêmes pensées, partagez les sentiments les uns des autres, aimez-vous comme des {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, ayez un cœur plein de tendresse et un esprit humble. \v 9 Ne rendez pas le mal pour le mal, ni l’insulte pour l’insulte. Au contraire, bénissez, car c’est à cela que vous avez été appelés, afin d’hériter une bénédiction.
fr.R: Enfin, vous tous, soyez d’accord les uns avec les autres et faites attention à ce que ressentent les autres. Aimez-vous comme des {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}. Soyez bons et doux, et ne vous croyez pas supérieurs aux autres. \v 9 Quand quelqu’un vous fait du mal, ne lui rendez pas le mal. Quand quelqu’un vous insulte, ne l’insultez pas en retour. Au contraire, demandez à Dieu de le bénir. Dieu vous a appelés à vivre ainsi, pour que vous receviez vous-mêmes la bénédiction de Dieu.

sw.L: Mwisho, nyote [kuweni] wenye nia moja, mnaoshiriki hisia za wengine, mnaopenda ndugu, wenye mioyo myororo, wenye mawazo ya unyenyekevu, \v 9 bila kurudisha ubaya kwa ubaya au tusi kwa tusi, bali kinyume chake mkibariki, kwa sababu mliitwa kwa ajili ya jambo hili, ili mpate kurithi baraka.
sw.B: Kwa ufupi: ninyi nyote mwe na umoja wa mawazo, mshiriki hisia za wenzenu, mpendane kama ndugu, mwe na mioyo ya huruma na mawazo ya unyenyekevu. \v 9 Msimlipe mtu ubaya kwa ubaya wala matusi kwa matusi. Badala yake, wabarikini, kwa sababu Mungu aliwaita kwa ajili hiyo, ili mrithi baraka.
sw.R: Mwisho, nyote mkubaliane ninyi kwa ninyi na mjali hisia za wenzenu. Pendaneni kama ndugu. Kuweni wapole na wenye huruma, wala msijione kuwa bora kuliko wengine. \v 9 Mtu akiwatendea ubaya, msimlipe ubaya. Mtu akiwatukana, msimtukane naye. Badala yake, mwombeni Mungu ambariki. Mungu aliwaita muishi hivyo, ili ninyi wenyewe mpokee baraka ya Mungu.

decisions.choice: finally: closing the household instructions and turning to the whole church
decisions.reason: Τὸ δὲ τέλος is used as an adverb, "finally" or "to sum up". πάντες, "all", widens the instructions of 2:13-3:7 to everyone. There is no verb; the adjectives and participles serve as commands, as in 3:1 and 3:7.

decisions.choice: five qualities of life together in the church
decisions.reason: ὁμόφρονες: agreeing in mind and purpose. συμπαθεῖς: feeling with others. φιλάδελφοι: loving fellow believers as family (1:22). εὔσπλαγχνοι: compassionate, literally "good-hearted" (Ephesians 4:32). ταπεινόφρονες: humble, not thinking too much of oneself (5:5).

decisions.choice: do not repay evil for evil, but bless: the teaching of Jesus, followed by Jesus himself
decisions.reason: Jesus told his followers to bless those who curse them (Luke 6:28; Matthew 5:44), and Paul passes on the same teaching (Romans 12:14, 12:17). Peter has just described Christ, who did not insult in return when he was insulted (2:23, where the verb shares the root of λοιδορίαν).

decisions.choice: bless: speak well of them and ask God's good for them
decisions.reason: εὐλογοῦντες means to speak well of someone, and with people as the object, to call down God's good on them. It answers "insult" in the same clause.

decisions.choice: called for this: to bless instead of retaliating
alternatives: called for this: to inherit a blessing, the purpose clause that follows
decisions.reason: εἰς τοῦτο can point back to blessing others or forward to the ἵνα clause. In 2:21 the same words point back to the suffering just described, which favors pointing back here: they were called to bless, so that they would inherit a blessing.

decisions.choice: inherit a blessing: receive from God the blessing he has promised his people
decisions.reason: Inheriting is how the letter speaks of the salvation kept for believers (1:4). Those who bless others will themselves be blessed by God, as the Psalm quoted next says (3:10-12).

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The word means love for fellow believers, women and men. "Brothers" stays available as the traditional form.

decisions.choice: ask God to bless them
decisions.reason: Readable says what blessing people means (m4) and names those to be blessed, the people who did wrong.

decisions.choice: hermanos, no setting
decisions.reason: As in Romans and Philippians, Spanish "hermanos" already covers brothers and sisters, so adding "y hermanas" would add words the Greek does not have, and there is no gender span where the English has one.

decisions.choice: ndugu, no setting
alternatives: ndugu wa kiume na wa kike
decisions.reason: "Ndugu" already means brothers and sisters, so Swahili needs no gender span where the English has one; the only traditional alternative would add "wa kiume" (male) and change the meaning.

source.text: ὁ γὰρ θέλων ζωὴν ἀγαπᾶν καὶ ἰδεῖν ἡμέρας ἀγαθὰς παυσάτω τὴν γλῶσσαν ἀπὸ κακοῦ καὶ χείλη τοῦ μὴ λαλῆσαι δόλον, ἐκκλινάτω δὲ ἀπὸ κακοῦ καὶ ποιησάτω ἀγαθόν, ζητησάτω εἰρήνην καὶ διωξάτω αὐτήν·

records.literal_gloss: The [one] for wanting life to love and to see days good, let him stop the tongue from evil and lips of the not to speak deceit, \v 11 and let him turn away from evil and let him do good, let him seek peace and let him pursue it;

en.L: For the one who wants to love life and to see good days, let {{gender:that person|him}} stop the tongue from evil and the lips from speaking deceit, \v 11 and let {{gender:that person|him}} turn away from evil and do good; let {{gender:that person|him}} seek peace and pursue it.
en.B: For whoever wants to love life and see good days must hold back the tongue from evil and the lips from speaking deceit, \v 11 must turn away from evil and do good, must look for peace and go after it.
en.R: The Scriptures say: Anyone who wants to love life and enjoy good days must stop saying evil things and telling lies. \v 11 {{gender:They|He}} must turn away from evil and do what is good. {{gender:They|He}} must look for peace and work hard to have it.

es.L: Porque el que quiere amar la vida y ver días buenos, detenga su lengua del mal y sus labios de hablar engaño; \v 11 apártese del mal y haga el bien; busque la paz y persígala.
es.B: Porque quien quiera amar la vida y ver días buenos debe contener su lengua del mal y sus labios de decir engaños; \v 11 debe apartarse del mal y hacer el bien, debe buscar la paz e ir tras ella.
es.R: Las Escrituras dicen: Quien quiera amar la vida y disfrutar de días buenos debe dejar de decir cosas malas y de contar mentiras. \v 11 Debe alejarse del mal y hacer lo bueno. Debe buscar la paz y esforzarse por tenerla.

fr.L: Car celui qui veut aimer la vie et voir des jours heureux, qu’il garde sa langue du mal et ses lèvres de dire la tromperie, \v 11 qu’il se détourne du mal et fasse le bien, qu’il cherche la paix et la poursuive.
fr.B: Car celui qui veut aimer la vie et voir des jours heureux doit garder sa langue du mal et ses lèvres des paroles trompeuses, \v 11 il doit se détourner du mal et faire le bien, chercher la paix et la poursuivre.
fr.R: Les Écritures disent : Celui qui veut aimer la vie et connaître des jours heureux doit arrêter de dire du mal et de mentir. \v 11 Il doit se détourner du mal et faire ce qui est bien. Il doit chercher la paix et faire tous ses efforts pour l’avoir.

sw.L: Kwa maana anayetaka kupenda uzima na kuona siku njema, auzuie ulimi [wake] kutoka kwa ubaya na midomo [yake] kutoka kunena udanganyifu; \v 11 ageuke mbali na ubaya na kutenda wema; aitafute amani na kuikimbilia.
sw.B: Kwa maana yeyote anayetaka kupenda uzima na kuona siku njema, lazima azuie ulimi wake na maovu na midomo yake na maneno ya udanganyifu; \v 11 lazima aache maovu na kutenda mema, aitafute amani na kuikimbilia.
sw.R: Maandiko yanasema: Mtu anayetaka kuyapenda maisha na kufurahia siku njema, lazima aache kusema maneno mabaya na kudanganya. \v 11 Lazima aache ubaya na kufanya yaliyo mema. Lazima atafute amani na kujitahidi sana kuipata.

decisions.choice: a quotation of Psalm 34:13-15, continuing in 3:12
decisions.reason: Peter quotes the psalm in the form of the Greek Old Testament, with small changes. The psalm asks a question ("Who is the one who wants life?") and gives commands to "you"; Peter turns them into a statement and third-person commands. He has already drawn on this psalm in 2:3 (Psalm 34:9). The quotation gives the reason for blessing instead of repaying evil (3:9).

decisions.choice: to love life and see good days: to have a life that is good, now and in the life to come
alternatives: a long life on earth only
decisions.reason: In the psalm this is a full and blessed life. In 1 Peter, life is also the "grace of life" (3:7) and the inheritance to come (1:4; 3:9), so the promise reaches beyond this life.

decisions.choice: deceit: lying and trickery in speech
decisions.reason: δόλον is cunning or deceit. The readers are told to put it away in 2:1, and 2:22 says that none was found in Christ's mouth.

decisions.choice: seek peace and pursue it: work actively for peace with others
decisions.reason: διωξάτω means to chase or run after something. Peace here is right relations with others, which a person must go after, not just wait for.

decisions.choice: {{gender:that person|him}}
decisions.reason: The Greek third-person command speaks of anyone at all. Literal keeps the form "let ... " with an inclusive default and "him" as the traditional alternative.

decisions.choice: whoever ... must
decisions.reason: Balanced turns the third-person commands into one sentence with "must", which needs no pronoun.

decisions.choice: The Scriptures say
decisions.reason: Readable tells the reader that this is a quotation (m1); a reader of the Greek would have recognized the psalm.

decisions.choice: {{gender:They|He}}
decisions.reason: The psalm speaks of anyone, woman or man.

decisions.choice: no gender span
decisions.reason: The English needs a pronoun for the third-person commands and puts it under the gender setting. Spanish says "detenga", "apártese", "debe" with no pronoun, so there is nothing for the setting to change.

decisions.choice: celui qui … qu’il, il, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The English needs {{gender:that person|him}} and {{gender:They|He}}. French "celui qui" already means anyone, and the "il" that refers back to it is generic French, so no span is added (style guide, section 7).

decisions.choice: uzima (L, B); maisha (R); no gender span
decisions.reason: "Uzima" is life itself, the word used for the life God gives, which fits the meaning decision that the promise reaches beyond this life; Readable says "maisha", the everyday word. The verb prefix a- has no gender, so Swahili has no counterpart to the English gender spans.

source.text: ὅτι ὀφθαλμοὶ κυρίου ἐπὶ δικαίους καὶ ὦτα αὐτοῦ εἰς δέησιν αὐτῶν, πρόσωπον δὲ κυρίου ἐπὶ ποιοῦντας κακά.

records.literal_gloss: Because eyes of Lord [are] on righteous [ones] and ears of him toward prayer of them, but face of Lord [is] upon [ones] doing evil [things].

en.L: Because [the] eyes of [the] Lord [are] on [the] righteous, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ears toward their prayer, but [the] face of [the] Lord [is] against those doing evil [things].
en.B: For the Lord keeps {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} eyes on the righteous and turns {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ears to their prayer, but the Lord's face is set against those who do evil.
en.R: The Lord watches over people who do what is right, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} listens when they pray. But the Lord is against those who do evil.

es.L: Porque [los] ojos del Señor [están] sobre [los] justos, y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} oídos [atentos] a su súplica, pero [el] rostro del Señor [está] contra los que hacen el mal.
es.B: Porque el Señor tiene {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} ojos puestos en los justos e inclina {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} oídos a su oración, pero el rostro del Señor se vuelve contra los que hacen el mal.
es.R: El Señor cuida a los que hacen lo que es justo, y escucha cuando oran. Pero el Señor está en contra de los que hacen el mal.

fr.L: Car les yeux du Seigneur [sont] sur les justes, et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} oreilles vers leur prière, mais la face du Seigneur [est] contre ceux qui font le mal.
fr.B: Car le Seigneur garde {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} yeux sur les justes et tourne {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} oreilles vers leur prière, mais la face du Seigneur s’oppose à ceux qui font le mal.
fr.R: Le Seigneur veille sur ceux qui font ce qui est juste, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} écoute quand ils prient. Mais le Seigneur est contre ceux qui font le mal.

sw.L: Kwa sababu macho ya Bwana [yako] juu ya wenye haki, na masikio {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} [yako] kwenye maombi yao, lakini uso wa Bwana [uko] dhidi ya wale wanaotenda maovu.
sw.B: Kwa maana Bwana huwaangalia wenye haki kwa macho {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, na hutega masikio {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kwa maombi yao, lakini uso wa Bwana unawapinga wale wanaotenda maovu.
sw.R: Bwana huwalinda watu wanaotenda yaliyo haki, na huwasikiliza wanapoomba. Lakini Bwana yuko kinyume na wale wanaotenda maovu.

decisions.choice: the end of the quotation of Psalm 34: verses 16-17a
decisions.reason: In the psalm, "Lord" stands for the divine name of God, YHWH; the Greek Old Testament and Peter have κύριος. Peter stops before the rest of Psalm 34:17, which says the Lord will cut off the memory of evildoers from the earth. The text does not say why he stops there.

decisions.choice: the Lord: God, as in the psalm; the letter may also hear it of Christ
decisions.reason: In 2:3-4 Peter applies an earlier line of the same psalm ("the Lord is good") to Christ. Here the Lord is the God of the psalm, and nothing in the sentence limits it further.

decisions.choice: eyes and ears on the righteous: God's watchful care and attention; his face against evildoers: his opposition
decisions.reason: The same preposition, ἐπὶ, is used both times, but the contrast with δὲ shows that the Lord's face is turned against those who do evil, as in Leviticus 17:10. His eyes on the righteous mean protection; his ears open to their prayer recall 3:7.

decisions.choice: against
decisions.reason: Literal follows the Greek elsewhere but says "against" here, so that the contrast in m3 is not lost.

decisions.choice: watches over ... listens ... is against
decisions.reason: Readable says what the pictures of eyes, ears and face mean (m3).

source.text: Καὶ τίς ὁ κακώσων ὑμᾶς ἐὰν τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ ζηλωταὶ γένησθε;

records.literal_gloss: And who [is] the [one] who will harm you if of the good zealous [ones] you become?

en.L: And who [is] the [one] who will harm you if you become zealous for the good?
en.B: And who will do you harm if you are devoted to doing what is good?
en.R: If you really want to do good, who is going to hurt you?

es.L: ¿Y quién [es] el que {{plural_you:les|os}} hará daño si {{plural_you:llegan|llegáis}} a ser celosos del bien?
es.B: ¿Y quién {{plural_you:les|os}} hará daño si {{plural_you:se dedican|os dedicáis}} con empeño a hacer el bien?
es.R: Si de verdad {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}} hacer el bien, ¿quién {{plural_you:les|os}} va a hacer daño?

fr.L: Et qui [est] celui qui vous fera du mal, si vous devenez zélés pour le bien ?
fr.B: Et qui vous fera du mal si vous vous appliquez avec ardeur à faire le bien ?
fr.R: Si vous voulez vraiment faire le bien, qui va vous faire du mal ?

sw.L: Na ni nani atakayewadhuru ninyi ikiwa mtakuwa wenye bidii kwa [yaliyo] mema?
sw.B: Na ni nani atakayewatendea ubaya ikiwa mmejitoa kutenda mema?
sw.R: Ikiwa kweli mnataka kutenda mema, ni nani atakayewadhuru?

decisions.choice: a question expecting the answer "no one", in the sense that no one can do them real harm
alternatives: a promise that believers who do good will never suffer
decisions.reason: The next sentence says at once that they may suffer for doing right (3:14). So the question does not promise freedom from suffering. It means that people generally do not punish those who do good (2:14), and that no one can harm them in the end, since God is with them (3:12). Isaiah 50:9 asks a similar question: who will harm me?

decisions.choice: zealous: eager, devoted
decisions.reason: ζηλωταὶ is one who is eager or devoted to something. Here it is the good, the conduct the letter has been describing since 2:12.

source.text: ἀλλ’ εἰ καὶ πάσχοιτε διὰ δικαιοσύνην, μακάριοι.

records.literal_gloss: But if even you should suffer because of righteousness, blessed.

en.L: But even if you should suffer because of righteousness, [you are] blessed.
en.B: But suppose you do suffer because of righteousness: even then you are blessed.
en.R: But even if you suffer for living a righteous life, you are still blessed.

es.L: Pero aun si {{plural_you:sufrieran|sufrierais}} por causa de [la] justicia, [{{plural_you:son|sois}}] bienaventurados.
es.B: Pero supongamos que {{plural_you:sufren|sufrís}} por causa de la justicia: aun así {{plural_you:son|sois}} bienaventurados.
es.R: Pero aunque {{plural_you:sufran|sufráis}} por vivir con justicia, Dios {{plural_you:los|os}} sigue bendiciendo.

fr.L: Mais même si vous deviez souffrir à cause de la justice, [vous êtes] bienheureux.
fr.B: Mais supposons que vous souffriez à cause de la justice : même alors, vous êtes bienheureux.
fr.R: Mais même si vous souffrez parce que vous menez une vie juste, Dieu vous bénit quand même.

sw.L: Lakini hata kama mngeteseka kwa sababu ya haki, [ninyi ni] heri.
sw.B: Lakini tuseme mnateseka kwa sababu ya haki: hata hivyo ninyi ni heri.
sw.R: Lakini hata kama mnateseka kwa sababu mnaishi maisha ya haki, bado Mungu anawabariki.

decisions.choice: even if you should suffer: a real possibility, but not the normal outcome
decisions.reason: πάσχοιτε is an optative, a mood used for something that might happen. Peter does not say they will always suffer for doing good, but that it may come (1:6; 4:12).

decisions.choice: righteousness: doing what is right in God's sight
decisions.reason: In 1 Peter δικαιοσύνην is right living (2:24). To suffer because of it is to suffer for doing good, as 3:17 says.

decisions.choice: blessed: an echo of Jesus' words in Matthew 5:10
decisions.reason: Jesus said that those persecuted because of righteousness are blessed (Matthew 5:10). μακάριοι means favored by God and truly well off, whatever the circumstances.

decisions.choice: for living a righteous life
decisions.reason: Readable says what righteousness means here (m2) and keeps the key word.

decisions.choice: bienaventurados (L, B); Dios los sigue bendiciendo (R)
decisions.reason: As in Romans 14:22 and James 1:12, μακάριοι is "bienaventurados", the word of Jesus' beatitudes that this verse echoes (meaning decision). Readable says what it means: God's favor rests on them.

decisions.choice: bienheureux (L, B); Dieu vous bénit (R); the same in 4:14
decisions.reason: "Heureux" today says "happy", a feeling; the word means the favour God gives, as in Jesus' beatitudes (m3). "Bienheureux" keeps that sense at Literal and Balanced, and Readable names God as the one who blesses.

decisions.choice: heri (L, B); Mungu anawabariki (R)
decisions.reason: As in Romans 14:22 and James 1:12, μακάριοι is "heri", the word of Jesus' beatitudes; Readable says plainly that God blesses them.

source.text: τὸν δὲ φόβον αὐτῶν μὴ φοβηθῆτε μηδὲ ταραχθῆτε, κύριον δὲ τὸν Χριστὸν ἁγιάσατε ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν, ἕτοιμοι ἀεὶ πρὸς ἀπολογίαν παντὶ τῷ αἰτοῦντι ὑμᾶς λόγον περὶ τῆς ἐν ὑμῖν ἐλπίδος, ἀλλὰ μετὰ πραΰτητος καὶ φόβου, συνείδησιν ἔχοντες ἀγαθήν, ἵνα ἐν ᾧ καταλαλεῖσθε καταισχυνθῶσιν οἱ ἐπηρεάζοντες ὑμῶν τὴν ἀγαθὴν ἐν Χριστῷ ἀναστροφήν.

records.literal_gloss: And the fear of them do not fear nor be troubled, \v 15 but [as] Lord the Christ sanctify in the hearts of you, ready always for a defense to everyone asking you a word about the in you hope, \v 16 but with gentleness and fear, a conscience having good, so that in which you are spoken against may be put to shame the [ones] abusing your good in Christ conduct.

en.L: And do not fear their fear, nor be troubled, \v 15 but in your hearts set apart the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} as Lord, [being] always ready [to make] a defense to everyone who asks you [for] an account of the hope [that is] in you, \v 16 yet with gentleness and fear, having a good conscience, so that in the [matter in] which you are spoken against, those who abuse your good conduct in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} may be put to shame.
en.B: Do not be afraid of what they threaten, and do not be shaken. \v 15 Instead, in your hearts set {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} apart as the holy Lord. Be ready at all times to make your defense to anyone who asks you for the reason behind the hope you hold. \v 16 Yet answer with gentleness and with reverence for God, keeping a good conscience, so that when people speak evil of you, those who insult your good life in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} will be ashamed.
en.R: Do not be afraid of the people who threaten you, and do not be upset. \v 15 Instead, deep in your hearts, honor {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} as the holy Lord. People may ask you why you have such hope. Always be ready to give them an answer. \v 16 But answer them gently, and with respect for God. Keep your conscience clean. Then when people say bad things about you, they will be ashamed, because they have spoken against the good way you live as followers of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

es.L: Y no {{plural_you:teman|temáis}} el temor de ellos ni {{plural_you:se turben|os turbéis}}, \v 15 sino {{plural_you:santifiquen|santificad}} en {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} corazones {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}} como Señor, [estando] siempre preparados para [dar] una defensa a todo el que {{plural_you:les|os}} pida cuenta de la esperanza que [hay] en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, \v 16 pero con mansedumbre y temor, teniendo buena conciencia, para que en lo que {{plural_you:son|sois}} calumniados, sean avergonzados los que difaman {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} buena conducta en {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}.
es.B: No {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} miedo de lo que ellos amenazan, ni {{plural_you:se inquieten|os inquietéis}}. \v 15 Más bien, {{plural_you:consagren|consagrad}} {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}} en {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} corazones como el Señor santo. {{plural_you:Estén|Estad}} siempre listos para defender{{plural_you:se|os}} ante cualquiera que {{plural_you:les|os}} pregunte el motivo de la esperanza que {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}}. \v 16 Pero {{plural_you:respondan|responded}} con mansedumbre y con reverencia a Dios, manteniendo una buena conciencia, para que, cuando hablen mal de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, queden avergonzados los que insultan {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} buena vida en {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}.
es.R: No {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} miedo de la gente que {{plural_you:los|os}} amenaza, y no {{plural_you:se preocupen|os preocupéis}}. \v 15 Más bien, en lo profundo de {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} corazón, {{plural_you:honren|honrad}} {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}} como el Señor santo. Puede que la gente {{plural_you:les|os}} pregunte por qué {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} tanta esperanza. {{plural_you:Estén|Estad}} siempre listos para responder. \v 16 Pero {{plural_you:respondan|responded}} con amabilidad y con respeto a Dios. {{plural_you:Mantengan|Mantened}} limpia {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} conciencia. Así, cuando la gente diga cosas malas de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, quedará avergonzada, porque ha hablado contra la buena manera en que {{plural_you:viven|vivís}} como seguidores {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}.

fr.L: Et ne craignez pas leur crainte, et ne soyez pas troublés, \v 15 mais sanctifiez dans vos cœurs le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} comme Seigneur, [étant] toujours prêts à [vous] défendre devant quiconque vous demande raison de l’espérance qui [est] en vous, \v 16 mais avec douceur et crainte, ayant une bonne conscience, afin que, là où l’on parle contre vous, ceux qui dénigrent votre bonne conduite {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} soient couverts de honte.
fr.B: Ne craignez pas leurs menaces et ne vous laissez pas ébranler. \v 15 Au contraire, dans vos cœurs, tenez le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} pour le Seigneur saint. Soyez toujours prêts à vous défendre devant quiconque vous demande la raison de l’espérance qui est en vous. \v 16 Mais faites-le avec douceur et avec respect pour Dieu, en gardant une bonne conscience, afin que, lorsqu’on dit du mal de vous, ceux qui insultent votre bonne conduite {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} soient couverts de honte.
fr.R: N’ayez pas peur des gens qui vous menacent, et ne vous inquiétez pas. \v 15 Au contraire, au fond de votre cœur, honorez le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} comme le Seigneur saint. Des gens vous demanderont peut-être pourquoi vous avez une telle espérance. Soyez toujours prêts à leur répondre. \v 16 Mais répondez-leur avec douceur, et avec respect pour Dieu. Gardez une conscience pure. Alors, quand des gens diront du mal de vous, ils auront honte, parce qu’ils auront critiqué la bonne manière dont vous vivez comme disciples du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.

sw.L: Basi hofu yao msiiogope, wala msitikiswe, \v 15 bali katika mioyo yenu mtakaseni {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} kuwa Bwana, [mkiwa] tayari wakati wote kutoa jibu la utetezi kwa kila mtu anayewaomba maelezo kuhusu tumaini lililomo ndani yenu, \v 16 ila pamoja na upole na hofu, mkiwa na dhamiri njema, ili katika jambo mnalosemwa vibaya, waone aibu wale wanaoudhihaki mwenendo wenu mwema ndani ya {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.B: Msiogope vitisho vyao, wala msitikisike. \v 15 Badala yake, katika mioyo yenu mkirini {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} kuwa Bwana mtakatifu. Mwe tayari wakati wote kujitetea mbele ya yeyote anayewauliza sababu ya tumaini mlilo nalo. \v 16 Lakini jibuni kwa upole na kwa kumcha Mungu, mkiwa na dhamiri njema, ili watu wanapowasema vibaya, wale wanaobeza maisha yenu mema katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} waone aibu.
sw.R: Msiwaogope watu wanaowatisha, wala msiwe na wasiwasi. \v 15 Badala yake, ndani kabisa ya mioyo yenu, mheshimuni {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} kama Bwana mtakatifu. Huenda watu wakawauliza kwa nini mna tumaini kubwa hivyo. Kuweni tayari siku zote kuwajibu. \v 16 Lakini wajibuni kwa upole, na kwa kumheshimu Mungu. Tunzeni dhamiri zenu ziwe safi. Kisha watu wanaposema mabaya juu yenu, wataona aibu, kwa sababu wamesema vibaya juu ya jinsi mnavyoishi vizuri kama wafuasi wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.

decisions.choice: an adaptation of Isaiah 8:12-13
decisions.reason: Isaiah was told not to fear what the people feared, but to treat the LORD of hosts as holy and to fear him. Peter takes the words from the Greek Old Testament, but where Isaiah has the Lord, the divine name in the Hebrew, Peter writes "the Christ": Christ is to be given the honor Isaiah gives to God.

decisions.choice: their fear: fear of them, of what the opponents threaten
alternatives: what they fear: do not share the fears of the unbelievers
decisions.reason: φόβον αὐτῶν can mean the fear they cause or the fear they feel. In Isaiah 8:12 it is what the people fear; in this letter, where the readers face hostile neighbors (3:16; 4:4), it most likely means the fear their opponents try to cause. The literal rendering keeps both readings open.

decisions.choice: set apart Christ as Lord: Lord is what they are to acknowledge him to be
alternatives: set apart the Lord Christ: Lord as a title alongside Christ
decisions.reason: κύριον has no article and stands apart from τὸν Χριστὸν, which suggests it says what Christ is to be to them. ἁγιάσατε is to treat as holy, to set apart as belonging to God, as in the prayer "hallowed be your name" (Matthew 6:9).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "the Christ"
alternatives: "the Lord God": God instead of Christ
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "God" here, the wording of Isaiah 8:13. The early manuscripts generally read "Christ", and a copyist was more likely to bring the text into line with Isaiah than to change it away from it. Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: defense ... account: an answer explaining their hope, whether in court or to a neighbor who asks
alternatives: a formal defense in court only
decisions.reason: ἀπολογίαν was used for a defense in court (Acts 25:16) but also for any reasoned answer. "Everyone who asks" includes informal questions. λόγον here means an account or reason.

decisions.choice: with gentleness and fear: gentle toward the questioner, reverent toward God
decisions.reason: φόβου in 1 Peter is reverence for God (1:17; 2:17; 3:2), and 3:14 has just told them not to fear people. Some take it as respect for the person asking; the letter's own use favors reverence for God.

decisions.choice: a good conscience: knowing before God that one has done right
decisions.reason: συνείδησιν is the inner awareness of right and wrong before God (2:19). Their lives should give the accusers nothing true to say.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "in which you are spoken against"
alternatives: "in which they speak against you as evildoers"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "they speak against you as evildoers", a wording that matches 2:12. The shorter text is found in important early manuscripts, and the longer one looks like a copyist's harmony with 2:12. The meaning is not changed. Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: in which: in the very matter for which they slander you, or when they do
decisions.reason: ἐν ᾧ can mean "in the matter in which" or "when"; the sense is the same: the slander will rebound on those who speak it.

decisions.choice: abuse: insult and mistreat; your good conduct in Christ: the way of life of people who belong to Christ
decisions.reason: ἐπηρεάζοντες is to insult or treat with spite (Luke 6:28). "In Christ" marks their conduct as that of people united to Christ.

decisions.choice: the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting. Literal keeps the article of the first one.

decisions.choice: set Christ apart as the holy Lord (B); honor Christ as the holy Lord (R)
decisions.reason: "Sanctify" is church language; Balanced and Readable say what treating someone as holy means.

decisions.choice: with reverence for God (B); with respect for God (R)
decisions.reason: Names whom the fear is toward (m6), so that readers do not take it as fear of the questioner.

decisions.choice: as followers of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Readable says what "in Christ" means for their conduct (m10).

decisions.choice: {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}}; {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}; {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}
decisions.reason: Title setting, as in Paul's letters: Spanish puts the article before "Mesías" but not before "Cristo", so the span takes in the preposition where "a el" or "de el" would contract.

decisions.choice: santifiquen (L); consagren (B); honren (R)
decisions.reason: "Apartar" in Spanish suggests putting something aside. "Consagrar" is to set apart as holy, which is what ἁγιάσατε means here.

decisions.choice: {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} for "in Christ" (here, 5:10 and 5:14)
decisions.reason: As in Colossians: French cannot say "en Messie", so the span covers the preposition, with the familiar "en Christ" as the default and "dans le Messie" as the alternative.

decisions.choice: mkirini ... kuwa Bwana mtakatifu
decisions.reason: "Kutenga" (set apart) would suggest putting Christ to one side. Balanced says "kukiri", to acknowledge him as the holy Lord; Literal keeps "kutakasa" and Readable says "kuheshimu".

source.text: κρεῖττον γὰρ ἀγαθοποιοῦντας, εἰ θέλοι τὸ θέλημα τοῦ θεοῦ, πάσχειν ἢ κακοποιοῦντας.

records.literal_gloss: Better for doing good, if should will the will of the God, to suffer than doing evil.

en.L: For [it is] better, if the will of God should will [it], to suffer doing good than doing evil.
en.B: It is better, after all, to suffer while doing good, if God wills that, than to suffer while doing wrong.
en.R: If it is God's will for you to suffer, it is better to suffer for doing good than for doing wrong.

es.L: Porque [es] mejor, si la voluntad de Dios [así lo] quisiera, sufrir haciendo el bien que haciendo el mal.
es.B: Después de todo, es mejor sufrir por hacer el bien, si Dios así lo quiere, que sufrir por hacer lo malo.
es.R: Si Dios quiere que {{plural_you:sufran|sufráis}}, es mejor sufrir por hacer el bien que por hacer lo malo.

fr.L: Car mieux [vaut], si la volonté de Dieu le voulait, souffrir en faisant le bien qu’en faisant le mal.
fr.B: Après tout, il vaut mieux souffrir en faisant le bien, si Dieu le veut, que souffrir en faisant le mal.
fr.R: Si Dieu veut que vous souffriez, il vaut mieux souffrir parce que vous faites le bien que parce que vous faites le mal.

sw.L: Kwa maana ni bora, kama mapenzi ya Mungu yangetaka [hivyo], kuteseka kwa kutenda mema kuliko kwa kutenda maovu.
sw.B: Baada ya yote, ni bora kuteseka kwa kutenda mema, kama Mungu anataka hivyo, kuliko kuteseka kwa kutenda mabaya.
sw.R: Ikiwa ni mapenzi ya Mungu mteseke, ni bora kuteseka kwa sababu ya kutenda mema kuliko kwa sababu ya kutenda mabaya.

decisions.choice: if God should will it: suffering is a possibility within God's will, not his constant plan for them
decisions.reason: θέλοι is optative, as in 3:14: if it should be so. The phrase, literally "if the will of God should will", places any suffering under God's control (4:19) without saying he wants it for its own sake.

decisions.choice: better: better before God, who approves the one who suffers for doing good
decisions.reason: κρεῖττον recalls 2:20: suffering for doing good is favor with God, while suffering for wrongdoing earns no credit. The next sentence gives the reason: Christ suffered as the righteous one (3:18).

decisions.choice: doing wrong
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the everyday word for the wrongdoing that could rightly be punished (2:14, 4:15).

source.text: ὅτι καὶ Χριστὸς ἅπαξ περὶ ἁμαρτιῶν ἔπαθεν, δίκαιος ὑπὲρ ἀδίκων, ἵνα ὑμᾶς προσαγάγῃ τῷ θεῷ, θανατωθεὶς μὲν σαρκὶ ζῳοποιηθεὶς δὲ πνεύματι· ἐν ᾧ καὶ τοῖς ἐν φυλακῇ πνεύμασιν πορευθεὶς ἐκήρυξεν, ἀπειθήσασίν ποτε ὅτε ἀπεξεδέχετο ἡ τοῦ θεοῦ μακροθυμία ἐν ἡμέραις Νῶε κατασκευαζομένης κιβωτοῦ εἰς ἣν ὀλίγοι, τοῦτ’ ἔστιν ὀκτὼ ψυχαί, διεσώθησαν δι’ ὕδατος.

records.literal_gloss: Because also Christ once for sins suffered, righteous for unrighteous, so that you he might bring to the God, having been put to death on the one hand in flesh, having been made alive on the other hand in spirit; \v 19 in which also to the in prison spirits having gone he proclaimed, \v 20 having disobeyed once, when was waiting the of the God patience in days of Noah, being prepared of an ark, into which a few, that is eight souls, were saved through water.

en.L: Because {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} also suffered once for sins, [the] righteous for [the] unrighteous, so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} might bring you to God, having been put to death in [the] flesh but made alive in [the] spirit; \v 19 in which also, having gone, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} proclaimed to the spirits in prison, \v 20 who once disobeyed, when the patience of God was waiting in [the] days of Noah while an ark was being prepared, into which a few, that is, eight souls, were saved through water.
en.B: For {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} also suffered for sins once for all, the righteous one for the unrighteous, so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} might lead you to God. In the flesh {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was put to death, but in the spirit {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was made alive. \v 19 In that spirit {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} also went and made a proclamation to the spirits in prison, \v 20 who had disobeyed long before, when God waited patiently in the days of Noah while the ark was being built. In that ark a few people, eight in all, came safely through the water.
en.R: {{christos:Christ|The Messiah}} also suffered, once and for all, to deal with sins. He was righteous, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} suffered for people who were not, so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} could bring you to God. He was put to death in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} human body, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was made alive in the spirit, raised to new life. \v 19 In the spirit {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} also went and announced a message to the spirits in prison. \v 20 Long ago, in the days of Noah, they had refused to obey God, while God waited patiently and Noah was building the ark. Only a few people, eight in all, went into the ark. They were saved as it carried them through the water.

es.L: Porque también {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} sufrió una vez por [los] pecados, [el] justo por [los] injustos, para llevar{{plural_you:los|os}} a Dios, habiendo sido muerto en [la] carne pero vivificado en [el] espíritu; \v 19 en el cual también, habiendo ido, proclamó a los espíritus en prisión, \v 20 que en otro tiempo desobedecieron, cuando la paciencia de Dios esperaba en [los] días de Noé, mientras se preparaba un arca, en la cual pocos, es decir, ocho almas, fueron salvados a través del agua.
es.B: Porque también {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} sufrió por los pecados una vez para siempre, el justo por los injustos, para conducir{{plural_you:los|os}} a Dios. En la carne se le dio muerte, pero en el espíritu fue vivificado. \v 19 En ese espíritu fue también e hizo una proclamación a los espíritus en prisión, \v 20 que habían desobedecido mucho tiempo antes, cuando Dios esperaba con paciencia en los días de Noé, mientras se construía el arca. En ella se salvaron unas pocas personas, ocho en total, pasando a través del agua.
es.R: {{christos:Cristo|El Mesías}} también sufrió por los pecados, una vez y para siempre. Él era justo, y sufrió por personas que no lo eran, para poder llevar{{plural_you:los|os}} a Dios. En {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} cuerpo humano le dieron muerte, pero en el espíritu recibió vida: fue resucitado a una vida nueva. \v 19 En el espíritu fue también y anunció un mensaje a los espíritus en prisión. \v 20 Hace mucho tiempo, en los días de Noé, ellos se habían negado a obedecer a Dios, mientras Dios esperaba con paciencia y Noé construía el arca. Solo unas pocas personas, ocho en total, entraron en el arca. Fueron salvadas mientras el arca las llevaba a través del agua.

fr.L: Car le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} aussi a souffert une fois pour les péchés, juste pour des injustes, afin de vous amener à Dieu, ayant été mis à mort dans la chair, mais rendu vivant dans l’esprit ; \v 19 dans lequel aussi, étant allé, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a proclamé aux esprits en prison, \v 20 qui autrefois avaient désobéi, quand la patience de Dieu attendait, aux jours de Noé, pendant que l’arche était construite, dans laquelle un petit nombre, c’est-à-dire huit âmes, ont été sauvées à travers l’eau.
fr.B: Car le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} aussi a souffert pour les péchés, une fois pour toutes, {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} le juste pour les injustes, afin de vous conduire à Dieu. Dans la chair, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a été mis à mort, mais dans l’esprit, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a été rendu à la vie. \v 19 C’est dans cet esprit aussi qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est allé faire une proclamation aux esprits en prison, \v 20 qui avaient désobéi bien longtemps auparavant, quand Dieu attendait avec patience, aux jours de Noé, pendant que l’arche était construite. Dans cette arche, un petit nombre de personnes, huit en tout, sont passées saines et sauves à travers l’eau.
fr.R: Le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} aussi a souffert, une fois pour toutes, pour en finir avec les péchés. Il était juste, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a souffert pour des gens qui ne l’étaient pas, afin de pouvoir vous amener à Dieu. Il a été mis à mort dans {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} corps humain, mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a été rendu vivant dans l’esprit, relevé pour une vie nouvelle. \v 19 Dans l’esprit, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est aussi allé annoncer un message aux esprits en prison. \v 20 Il y a très longtemps, aux jours de Noé, ils avaient refusé d’obéir à Dieu, pendant que Dieu attendait avec patience et que Noé construisait l’arche. Seul un petit nombre de personnes, huit en tout, sont entrées dans l’arche. Elles ont été sauvées, car l’arche les a portées à travers l’eau.

sw.L: Kwa sababu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} pia aliteseka mara moja kwa ajili ya dhambi, mwenye haki kwa ajili ya wasio na haki, ili awalete ninyi kwa Mungu, akiwa ameuawa katika mwili lakini akahuishwa katika roho; \v 19 ambamo pia, akiwa amekwenda, aliwatangazia roho walio gerezani, \v 20 waliokataa kutii zamani, wakati uvumilivu wa Mungu ulipokuwa ukisubiri katika siku za Nuhu, wakati safina ikijengwa, ambamo wachache, yaani, nafsi nane, waliokolewa kupitia maji.
sw.B: Kwa maana {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} pia aliteseka kwa ajili ya dhambi mara moja tu kwa wakati wote, mwenye haki kwa ajili ya wasio na haki, ili awafikishe ninyi kwa Mungu. Aliuawa katika mwili, lakini akahuishwa katika roho. \v 19 Katika roho hiyo alikwenda pia akawatangazia roho walio gerezani, \v 20 ambao zamani walikuwa wamekataa kutii, wakati Mungu alipongoja kwa uvumilivu katika siku za Nuhu, safina ilipokuwa ikijengwa. Ndani ya safina hiyo watu wachache, wanane kwa jumla, walivuka maji salama.
sw.R: {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} pia aliteseka, mara moja tu kwa wakati wote, ili kushughulikia dhambi. Yeye alikuwa mwenye haki, naye aliteseka kwa ajili ya watu wasio na haki, ili aweze kuwaleta ninyi kwa Mungu. Aliuawa katika mwili {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wa kibinadamu, lakini akafanywa hai katika roho, akafufuliwa kwa uzima mpya. \v 19 Katika roho alikwenda pia akawatangazia ujumbe roho walio gerezani. \v 20 Zamani, katika siku za Nuhu, walikuwa wamekataa kumtii Mungu, wakati Mungu aliposubiri kwa uvumilivu na Nuhu alipokuwa akijenga safina. Watu wachache tu, wanane kwa jumla, waliingia ndani ya safina. Waliokolewa safina ilipowabeba juu ya maji.

decisions.choice: 3:18-20 is one record: the sentence goes on after the raised dot at the end of 3:18
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT puts a raised dot after πνεύματι, but 3:19 begins with a relative clause, ἐν ᾧ, "in which", that cannot stand on its own and most likely refers back to that word. The two verses are kept in one record so that the link, which matters for the meaning of 3:19, is visible. The token order is unchanged.

decisions.choice: Christ suffered once for all to deal with sins, the righteous one in place of the unrighteous
decisions.reason: ἅπαξ means once, never to be repeated (Hebrews 9:26-28). περὶ ἁμαρτιῶν recalls the Greek Old Testament's phrase for the sin offering (Leviticus 5:6-7). δίκαιος ὑπὲρ ἀδίκων echoes Isaiah 53:11, the righteous servant who bears the sins of many. "Also" ties Christ's suffering to the readers' (3:17): he too suffered unjustly.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "suffered" and "you"
decisions.reason: Some important manuscripts read "died" instead of "suffered", and some read "us" instead of "you". The letter speaks of Christ's suffering throughout (2:21, 4:1), which supports "suffered"; either way the suffering meant here ends in his death. Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: bring you to God: lead you into God's presence
decisions.reason: προσαγάγῃ is the word for bringing someone before a king or bringing an offering to God. Christ's death opens the way to God for those who were far off (2:9-10, 2:25).

decisions.choice: in the flesh ... in the spirit: two spheres of existence, mortal human life and the new life of resurrection
alternatives: his body died but his human spirit lived on
made alive by the Holy Spirit
decisions.reason: σαρκὶ and πνεύματι are set against each other with μὲν ... δὲ. Christ was put to death as a mortal man; God made him alive, raising him from the dead (1:3, 1:21; 3:21). The contrast is between two kinds of existence, as in Romans 1:3-4 and 1 Timothy 3:16, not between a body that died and a soul that did not. Whether "spirit" names God's Spirit directly or the spiritual mode of Christ's risen life cannot be settled from the grammar.

decisions.choice: in which: in that spirit, in his risen state
decisions.reason: ἐν ᾧ most naturally refers back to the last word, πνεύματι: in the sphere of the spirit Christ also went. It may also mean "at which time" or "and so".

decisions.choice: the spirits in prison: an open question; most likely the rebellious spiritual beings of Noah's time
alternatives: the people who died in the flood, now dead
the people of Noah's day, preached to through Noah while they were alive
decisions.reason: πνεύμασιν without further description usually means non-human spirits in the New Testament (though Hebrews 12:23 uses it of the human dead). Jewish writings of the time, and 2 Peter 2:4-5 and Jude 6, speak of angels who sinned before the flood (Genesis 6:1-4) being held in prison until judgment. Others take the spirits as the people who died in the flood, a reading linked with 4:6, or as Noah's generation, to whom Christ spoke through Noah. The text says only that they were in prison and had disobeyed in Noah's days.

decisions.choice: having gone, he proclaimed: after being made alive, Christ went and announced a message; the text does not say what it was
alternatives: he went down to the place of the dead between his death and resurrection
he preached the gospel to offer them a second chance
