decisions.reason: πορευθεὶς is the same participle used in 3:22 of Christ going into heaven, which suggests a journey of the risen Christ. ἐκήρυξεν means to announce as a herald; it is used for preaching the gospel, but it can also announce victory or judgment, and the letter does not use its usual word for preaching good news here. The text does not say where the prison is, what Christ announced, or how the spirits responded. It does not teach that the dead are given another chance to repent, and it does not say that Christ descended to hell.

decisions.choice: the flood: Genesis 6-8
decisions.reason: God's patience waited while the ark was built (Genesis 6:3, 6:14-22). Eight people were in the ark: Noah, his wife, his three sons and their wives (Genesis 7:13). ψυχαί here means people, persons (Acts 27:37). The few who were saved are a picture of the small, threatened churches Peter writes to.

decisions.choice: saved through water: they came safely through the flood, and the water that carried the ark was the means of their rescue
alternatives: through the water only as a place they passed through
by means of the water only
decisions.reason: δι with ὕδατος can mean passing through the water or by means of it. Both fit: the water destroyed the world, yet bore up the ark. Peter's next words make the water a picture of baptism (3:21).

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: proclaimed (L); made a proclamation (B); announced a message (R)
decisions.reason: "Preached" would suggest that he preached the gospel to them, which the text does not say (m8). These words keep the question open, as the Greek does.

decisions.choice: in the flesh ... in the spirit, lowercase
alternatives: in the body ... in the Spirit
decisions.reason: The words keep the open question in m5; "Spirit" with a capital would decide it.

decisions.choice: in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} human body ... in the spirit, raised to new life
alternatives: in the flesh ... in the spirit
decisions.reason: Readable explains "flesh" as human bodily life and "made alive" as resurrection (m5). This explanation follows the most likely reading and leaves the meaning of "spirit" open.

decisions.choice: once for all (B); once and for all (R); Noah was building (R); people (B, R)
alternatives: once; while an ark was being prepared; souls
decisions.reason: "Once for all" says what "once" means here (m2). Readable names Noah as the builder (Genesis 6:14-22). "People" is the sense of "souls" (m9).

decisions.choice: sufrir
decisions.reason: The same Greek verb is used of the readers in 3:14 and 3:17 and of Christ here. Spanish uses "sufrir" every time, so the reader sees that Christ suffered as they may suffer; "padecer" is the older word familiar from Spanish Bibles.

decisions.choice: afin de vous amener (L); afin de vous conduire (B)
decisions.reason: French can use the infinitive when the subject is the same, which is lighter than a second clause with "il"; the meaning is unchanged, Christ is the one who brings them to God (m4).

decisions.choice: roho (spirit, lowercase; and the spirits); nafsi (L) and watu (B, R) for ψυχαί
decisions.reason: Swahili "roho" is both spirit and soul. It renders πνεύματι, lowercase so as not to decide the question the meaning decision leaves open, and the spirits in prison. For ψυχαί, which here means persons, Literal says "nafsi" and Balanced and Readable "watu", so that the eight are not confused with the spirits.

decisions.choice: aliwatangazia
decisions.reason: "Kuhubiri" is the word for preaching the gospel, which the text does not say Christ did here (meaning decision). "Kutangaza" (announce, proclaim) keeps the question open, as the Greek does.

source.text: ὃ καὶ ὑμᾶς ἀντίτυπον νῦν σῴζει βάπτισμα, οὐ σαρκὸς ἀπόθεσις ῥύπου ἀλλὰ συνειδήσεως ἀγαθῆς ἐπερώτημα εἰς θεόν, δι’ ἀναστάσεως Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὅς ἐστιν ἐν δεξιᾷ θεοῦ πορευθεὶς εἰς οὐρανὸν ὑποταγέντων αὐτῷ ἀγγέλων καὶ ἐξουσιῶν καὶ δυνάμεων.

records.literal_gloss: Which also you, antitype, now saves, baptism, not of flesh a putting away of filth but of a conscience good a pledge toward God, through resurrection of Jesus Christ, \v 22 who is at right [hand] of God, having gone into heaven, having been subjected to him angels and authorities and powers.

en.L: Which also now saves you, [as] an antitype: baptism, not a putting away of filth from [the] flesh but a pledge of a good conscience toward God, through [the] resurrection of Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, \v 22 who is at [the] right hand of God, having gone into heaven, angels and authorities and powers having been made subject to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: This water points ahead to baptism, which now saves you as well. Baptism is not washing dirt off the body, but the pledge of a good conscience made to God. It saves you through the resurrection of Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. \v 22 He went into heaven and is now at God's right hand, and angels, authorities, and powers have been made subject to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: That water was a picture of baptism, which now saves you too. Baptism does not save you by washing dirt from your body. In baptism you make a promise to God from a good conscience. Baptism saves you because Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} rose from the dead. \v 22 He has gone into heaven and is at God's right hand, the place of highest honor and power. Angels and all authorities and powers have been made to obey {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Lo cual también ahora {{plural_you:los|os}} salva a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, [como] antitipo: [el] bautismo, no [como] eliminación de [la] suciedad de [la] carne, sino [como] compromiso de una buena conciencia hacia Dios, por medio de [la] resurrección de {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, \v 22 que está a [la] diestra de Dios, habiendo ido al cielo, sometidos a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} ángeles y autoridades y poderes.
es.B: Esa agua anticipa el bautismo, que ahora {{plural_you:los|os}} salva también a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. El bautismo no es quitar la suciedad del cuerpo, sino el compromiso que una buena conciencia hace con Dios. {{plural_you:Los|Os}} salva por medio de la resurrección de {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}. \v 22 Él subió al cielo y ahora está a la diestra de Dios, y ángeles, autoridades y poderes han sido sometidos a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: Aquella agua era una figura del bautismo, que ahora {{plural_you:los|os}} salva también a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. El bautismo no {{plural_you:los|os}} salva por lavar la suciedad del cuerpo. En el bautismo {{plural_you:ustedes hacen|vosotros hacéis}} una promesa a Dios con una buena conciencia. El bautismo {{plural_you:los|os}} salva porque {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías,}} resucitó de entre los muertos. \v 22 Él ha ido al cielo y está a la derecha de Dios, el lugar de mayor honor y poder. Los ángeles y todas las autoridades y poderes han sido puestos bajo {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mando.

fr.L: Ce qui, comme antitype, vous sauve aussi maintenant, [c’est] le baptême, non l’enlèvement d’une saleté de la chair, mais l’engagement d’une bonne conscience envers Dieu, par la résurrection de Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, \v 22 qui est à la droite de Dieu, étant allé au ciel, les anges, les autorités et les puissances {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ayant été soumis.
fr.B: Cette eau annonçait le baptême, qui maintenant vous sauve, vous aussi. Le baptême, ce n’est pas enlever la saleté du corps, mais l’engagement d’une bonne conscience pris envers Dieu. Le baptême vous sauve par la résurrection de Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}. \v 22 Jésus est allé au ciel et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est maintenant à la droite de Dieu, et les anges, les autorités et les puissances {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont été soumis.
fr.R: Cette eau était une image du baptême, qui maintenant vous sauve, vous aussi. Le baptême ne vous sauve pas en lavant la saleté de votre corps. Dans le baptême, vous faites une promesse à Dieu avec une bonne conscience. Le baptême vous sauve parce que Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} est ressuscité d’entre les morts. \v 22 Il est allé au ciel, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est à la droite de Dieu, la place qui a le plus d’honneur et de pouvoir. Les anges et toutes les autorités et les puissances ont été obligés de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} obéir.

sw.L: Ambao pia sasa unawaokoa ninyi, kama mfano unaolingana [nayo]: ubatizo, si kuondolewa kwa uchafu wa mwili, bali ahadi ya dhamiri njema kwa Mungu, kupitia ufufuo wa Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, \v 22 ambaye yuko mkono wa kuume wa Mungu, akiwa amekwenda mbinguni, malaika na mamlaka na nguvu wakiwa wametiishwa chini {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.B: Maji hayo yanaashiria ubatizo, ambao sasa unawaokoa ninyi pia. Ubatizo si kuosha uchafu wa mwili, bali ni ahadi kwa Mungu itokayo katika dhamiri njema. Unawaokoa kupitia ufufuo wa Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}. \v 22 Yeye alikwenda mbinguni na sasa yuko mkono wa kuume wa Mungu, na malaika, mamlaka na nguvu wamewekwa chini {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.R: Maji yale yalikuwa picha ya ubatizo, ambao sasa unawaokoa ninyi pia. Ubatizo hauwaokoi kwa kuosha uchafu wa miili yenu. Katika ubatizo mnatoa ahadi kwa Mungu kutoka katika dhamiri safi. Ubatizo unawaokoa kwa sababu Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} alifufuka kutoka kwa wafu. \v 22 Ameenda mbinguni na yuko mkono wa kulia wa Mungu, mahali pa heshima na mamlaka ya juu kabisa. Malaika na wenye mamlaka wote na wenye nguvu wote wamefanywa wamtii.

decisions.choice: which ... antitype ... baptism: the water of the flood points ahead to baptism, which corresponds to it
alternatives: baptism is the antitype of the ark
which refers to the whole event of 3:20, not the water alone
decisions.reason: ὃ most likely refers back to the water of 3:20. ἀντίτυπον is something that corresponds to an earlier pattern; βάπτισμα names what that is. The grammar of the sentence is compressed and has been read in several ways, but on each the flood is a pattern and baptism its counterpart.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "you"
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read "us" instead of "you"; the pronouns are easily confused in Greek manuscripts. The meaning is the same. Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: baptism now saves you, through the resurrection of Jesus Christ
decisions.reason: The text says plainly that baptism saves, and says how: not as an outward washing, but through Christ's resurrection, the source of new birth (1:3), and as a response made to God. It does not say that water has power in itself, and it does not call baptism only a symbol. How baptism and faith are related is understood differently among churches; the translation reports what the text says.

decisions.choice: not a putting away of filth from the flesh: not an outward washing of the body
alternatives: not the removal of moral filth or sinful nature
decisions.reason: ῥύπου is dirt; σαρκὸς here is the body. Peter sets baptism apart from ordinary washing and from ritual baths that cleaned only the body.

decisions.choice: pledge: the commitment made to God from a good conscience
alternatives: an appeal to God for a good conscience
the answer of a good conscience to God
decisions.reason: ἐπερώτημα occurs only here in the New Testament. Its verb means to ask; the noun can mean a question, a request, or, in later Greek documents, a formal pledge given in answer to a question, as in agreeing to a contract. On that reading, baptism is the moment the believer answers God with a commitment. If it means a request, baptism is an appeal to God for a cleansed conscience. The genitive συνειδήσεως ἀγαθῆς fits either.

decisions.choice: at the right hand of God: the place of honor and authority promised in Psalm 110:1
decisions.reason: "Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies your footstool" (Psalm 110:1) is applied to Jesus throughout the New Testament (Acts 2:34-35; Hebrews 1:13).

decisions.choice: angels, authorities and powers: spiritual beings of every rank
decisions.reason: ἐξουσιῶν and δυνάμεων are used in the New Testament for spiritual powers (Romans 8:38; Ephesians 1:21; 1 Corinthians 15:24). ὑποταγέντων says they have been put under Christ; this may include the spirits of 3:19. The same participle πορευθεὶς "having gone" is used in 3:19.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT, without an addition found in Latin manuscripts
alternatives: after "right hand of God" add "swallowing up death, so that we might become heirs of eternal life"
decisions.reason: Some Latin manuscripts, and the Latin Vulgate, add these words after "right hand of God". They are not in the Greek manuscripts on which the SBLGNT is based. Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: This water points ahead to (B); That water was a picture of (R)
decisions.reason: Says what "antitype" means (m1) and names what "which" refers to.

decisions.choice: the place of highest honor and power
decisions.reason: Readable says what being at God's right hand means (m6).

decisions.choice: a new sentence for 3:22
alternatives: who is at the right hand of God, having gone into heaven ...
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable start a new sentence and put the going into heaven before the being at God's right hand, the order in which they happened.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}
decisions.reason: Title setting, as in Romans 1:1: the default is the usual Spanish form of the name, the alternative separates name and title.

decisions.choice: compromiso
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads ἐπερώτημα as a pledge given in answer to a question; "compromiso" says that. Older Spanish Bibles have "demanda", and "petición" would take the other reading, a request to God.

decisions.choice: Jésus est allé au ciel
decisions.reason: In French the previous sentence has "le baptême" as its subject, so a new sentence beginning "Il" would seem to speak of baptism. Balanced names Jesus, as the Greek relative pronoun points to him.

decisions.choice: ahadi
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads ἐπερώτημα as a pledge given in answer to a question; "ahadi" (promise, pledge) says that. "Ombi" would take the other reading, a request to God, and "jibu" (answer) loses the commitment.
